name: Kepler-88
title: Kepler-88: weighing a hidden planet by transit timing (real data)
notes: Real data: 119 mid-transit times of Kepler-88 b (KOI-142) from the Kepler TTV catalogue of Holczer et al. (2016). Its O − C swings by ±10 hours over 630 days: a planet near the 2:1 resonance pulls on it, though that planet never transits. The N-body fit samples planet c’s mass, period and phase and both eccentricities, with b’s own T0 and P profiled; c’s orbit is put at i = 87°. The catalogue errors are too small for this model, so 8.7 minutes of timing noise are added in quadrature. Compare c with Nesvorný et al. (2013) and Weiss et al. (2020) on the Methods page.

warnings: Most points (77%) were drawn by slice sampling, because region sampling was too slow here. Such runs scatter more in ln Z than the quoted error (up to about twice for thin, curved posteriors), and the balance between separate arms or modes of the posterior is less certain.
T mid (c) and √e sin ω are 0.99 correlated: the data constrain a combination of the two. Fix one, give one a tighter prior, or fit the combination.
T mid (c) and √e sin ω (c) are -0.98 correlated: the data constrain a combination of the two. Fix one, give one a tighter prior, or fit the combination.
√e sin ω and √e sin ω (c) are -0.98 correlated: the data constrain a combination of the two. Fix one, give one a tighter prior, or fit the combination.
